questions.stem: During incident response, what is the 'chain of custody,' and why does it matter?

choices.text: Documentation of exactly who handled the evidence and when, or it becomes useless in court
The order in which services restart after an outage
The list of approved software licenses

questions.explanation: Chain of custody is like a tracking number for evidence: you document exactly who touched it and when, or it becomes inadmissible in court.
questions.trap: It tracks evidence handling, not service restart order or backups.

questions.stem: Following the order of volatility (OOV), which data must you capture FIRST?

choices.text: CPU registers and cache (the most volatile data)

questions.explanation: Capture the most volatile data first - CPU registers and cache - before moving to less volatile data like the hard drive or backup tapes.
questions.trap: The hard drive and backup tapes are LEAST volatile; volatile data like registers and cache disappears fast and must be grabbed first.

questions.stem: When imaging a drive for evidence, what tool ensures you don't accidentally alter the original data?
questions.explanation: Make a bit-by-bit image of the entire drive using a write blocker so you don't alter the evidence.
questions.trap: A degausser would destroy the data; a write blocker preserves it by preventing any writes during imaging.

choices.text: The end-user license agreement that dictates how you may use the software
A non-disclosure agreement between two companies
An acceptable use policy for employees

questions.explanation: The EULA (end-user license agreement) is the long contract you click 'I agree' to; it dictates how you may use the software.
questions.trap: An NDA protects secrets between parties and an AUP governs employee tech use - the EULA is specifically the software-use contract.

questions.stem: Which license type allows a set number of people to use the software at the same time?
questions.explanation: A concurrent license allows a set number of simultaneous users. A per-seat license, by contrast, is tied to one specific person.
questions.trap: Per-seat is one named user; concurrent is a shared pool of simultaneous users.

questions.stem: What distinguishes open-source software (FOSS) from closed-source software?

choices.text: FOSS can only run on Linux
FOSS gives you the source code to modify, unlike closed source

questions.explanation: Open-source software (FOSS) provides the source code so you can modify it, unlike closed-source software where the code is hidden.
questions.trap: FOSS being open isn't about price or OS - it's about access to and the right to modify the source code.

questions.stem: Two companies want to share trade secrets while protecting them legally on both sides. Which agreement fits?
questions.explanation: An NDA (non-disclosure agreement) protects trade secrets; when both sides share secrets, it's a mutual NDA.
questions.trap: A EULA governs software use and an AUP governs employee behavior - protecting shared secrets between firms is the NDA.

questions.stem: Social Security numbers are an example of which category of regulated data?
questions.explanation: Personally identifiable information (PII) includes data like Social Security numbers that can identify an individual.
questions.trap: PHI is specifically health data and PCI-DSS covers payment cards; a Social Security number is general PII.

questions.stem: In healthcare, protected health information (PHI) is mandated by which regulation?
questions.explanation: PHI (protected health information) is mandated by HIPAA. Credit-card data follows PCI-DSS.
questions.trap: PCI-DSS governs payment cards, not health records; PHI is HIPAA's domain.

questions.stem: Which document limits a company's legal liability by defining what employees can and cannot do with company technology?
questions.explanation: An acceptable use policy (AUP) limits legal liability by spelling out exactly what employees may and may not do with company technology.
questions.trap: A EULA is between you and a software vendor; the internal rulebook for employee tech use is the AUP.
